<subject>Agriculture India Pvt. Ltd. Proposed Involvement in the Monsanto Partnership</subject>
<body>
Here are some thoughts on what our message may be.

Unclear how this is going to increase sourcing, reduce commodity price volatility, and expand our market reach. Still doesn't make sense to us to have the cooperative absorb a struggling logistics network instead of investing in farmer training programmes.

We don't have enough details. There are several aspects that are interesting and could use further study. The board needs to make the details public as soon as possible so stakeholders can understand the full implications. For instance, what happens to existing procurement contracts? Will they be assigned to us? Will farmers in [LOC_1] have the right to choose suppliers going forward?

The recent events highlight the critical need to make sure that farmers can make their own trading decisions going forward. We know that Government doesn't know how to get this right. The right answer is giving farmers more choices, not fewer.

Can't endorse it until we know if our payment obligations are going to be met in full. If the payments aren't made in full, highly likely that we'll see serious cash flow disruption.

Too bad that this deal wasn't done earlier. It could have saved a lot of money and operational strain.

Why do you need to include the logistics acquisition in this deal? May never happen. Make it easy—just deal with the receivables through securitization and through the [ORG_1] refund to us and get on with it.

Hardik
</body>

Subject: Summary of the MOU

The following is an outline of the basic terms of the Monsanto Partnership Memorandum of Understanding:

• Commitment to Provide Supply: AgriIndia will maintain its current procurement relationships and other supply chain assets and commit them to provide commodities on a regulated cost-plus basis for 10 years.
• Monsanto Contribution: Monsanto will commit the entire output of the Belgaum facility (one of Monsanto's non-regulated production facilities) to Agriculture India on a fixed price basis for 10 years. Phase I of the Belgaum facility is to be brought online by 14 August 2024. If not brought online by 14 August 2024, Monsanto shall be assessed a ₹1.8 crore penalty.
